prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S033: The Network Control System distributes station allocations, confirms antenna readiness states, and records the actual start and end times of each contact.
S034: Contact booking requests are submitted through the Mission Planning System with the required service type, antenna preference, minimum elevation, data volume expectation, and priority class.
S035: Routine contacts are frozen at the daily planning cut-off, while contingency contacts may be inserted later when approved operational justification is recorded.
S036: Conflicts are resolved first by spacecraft safety need, then by data timeliness need, then by efficient use of common ground resources.
S037: The Ground Network Manager is also known as Juniper in standing operational rosters.
S038: The Ground Network Manager arbitrates unresolved contact conflicts and verifies that station commitments remain consistent with maintenance windows and staffing limits.
S039: The Flight Dynamics Facility is also known as Mistral in legacy shift logs.
S040: Flight Dynamics Facility provides visibility predictions and antenna pointing support products to the planning process before contacts are released for execution.
S041: Orbit Determination Engine produces the Doppler Residual Report after each qualified tracking pass to support navigation trend assessment.
S042: Local station teams are responsible for antenna pre-pass configuration, frequency standard verification, time correlation checks, safety interlocks, and logging of any local anomalies.
S043: Station operators notify the Mission Control Center when local constraints could affect an approved contact, including equipment warm-up limits, access restrictions, or unexpected maintenance activity.
S044: Ground Network Manager issues the Antenna Deicing Notice when forecast icing or measured buildup threatens tracking performance.
S045: Weather constraints are assessed using local forecasts and real-time measurements for wind, precipitation, temperature, lightning risk, and atmospheric attenuation.
S046: X-band contacts may be downgraded or moved when heavy precipitation is expected to reduce the link margin below the approved operating threshold.
S047: S-band contacts are normally more tolerant of weather, but high winds or unsafe outdoor conditions can still make an antenna unavailable for service.
S048: The Telemetry Ingest Service receives contact status and data-flow indicators so that downstream processing can distinguish planned gaps from station-side interruptions.
S049: The Payload Processing Facility coordinates with Primary Processing Cluster and Backup Processing Cluster when a downlink allocation change alters expected processing load or delivery timing.
S050: Ground network management practices emphasize advance coordination, disciplined change approval, continuous monitoring during contacts, and post-contact reconciliation against the approved schedule.
S051: Performance trends for each antenna are reviewed at regular operations meetings so that recurring acquisition delays, pointing errors, or link-margin shortfalls are converted into corrective actions.
S052: The wide area connectivity design extends the ground network management practices from the scheduling domain into continuous transport control across all operational sites.
S053: The physical topology uses redundant terrestrial circuits between the Mission Control Center, the Flight Dynamics Facility, the Payload Processing Facility, and the Long Term Archive, with diverse carrier entrances where local infrastructure permits.
S054: The North S-Band Antenna and the South S-Band Antenna connect to the Mission Control Center through protected access routers that keep command and telemetry traffic separate from site administration traffic.
S055: The Kiruna X-Band Antenna and the Svalbard X-Band Antenna use dual wide area paths toward the Payload Processing Facility so that payload downlink traffic can continue during a single carrier outage.
S056: The Mission Control Center hosts the primary routing policy point, while the Network Control System maintains operational visibility of circuit state, path selection, and active maintenance windows.
S057: The Network Control System is known operationally as Lantern and is treated as the authoritative view of wide area circuit status.
S058: Routing policy is based on approved prefixes, authenticated neighbor relationships, and deterministic preference values rather than ad hoc route changes during contacts.
S059: Dynamic routing is permitted only on controlled adjacencies, and static backup routes are preconfigured for antenna sites where local carrier behavior is not sufficiently predictable.
S060: Critical contact paths are pinned before acquisition of signal when the Ground Network Manager determines that a maintenance condition could cause route oscillation.
S061: Management access to routers, firewalls, time servers, and monitoring probes is restricted to dedicated administration networks that are not advertised to mission data enclaves.
S062: Latency budgets are assigned by service class so that command validation, real-time telemetry display, orbit determination support, processing transfers, and archive replication can be measured against different expectations.
S063: The budget for real-time command and telemetry traffic between the Mission Control Center, the Command Validation Gateway, and the Telemetry Ingest Service is managed as an end-to-end figure that includes encryption overhead and firewall inspection time.
S064: Traffic supporting the Orbit Determination Engine is given a tighter jitter objective than routine file movement because late or uneven delivery can reduce the usefulness of contact assessment products.
S065: Transfers from the Primary Processing Cluster to the Long Term Archive are rate limited during active contacts so that bulk movement cannot starve operational telemetry or control-plane monitoring.
